GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA  
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1278 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
National Mission for Manuscripts 
 
 
1278. Shri Baijayant Panda: 
          Shri Murasoli S: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) the current status of implementation of the National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM) across the 
country, including the details of manuscript surveys conducted and digitisation undertaken during 
the last five years and the current year; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any evaluation or review of the Mission with regard to 
institutional capacity, regional coverage and utilisation of allocated funds; 
(c) if so, the key findings thereof; and 
(d) the details of the extent of coverage along with progress of the National Mission for Manuscripts 
in Odisha for preservation of Manuscripts from repositories in Tamil Nadu including Thanjavur 
district, particularly in the Saraswathi Mahal Library, along with the number of manuscripts 
identified, conserved and digitised, institutional partners involved and funds released thereon 
during the said period? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) Government has launched Gyan Bharatam Mission, subsuming erstwhile National Mission for 
Manuscripts (NMM), as a major initiative under the Ministry of Culture. It aims to survey, document, 
conserve, digitize and make accessible manuscripts located in academic institutions, museums, libraries, 
and private collections across India.National Manuscript Survey was launched in March, 2026 across all 
States and Union Territories of the country to identify and document manuscript holdings, repositories 
and custodians representing diverse languages and scripts.During the survey, more than 1.19 crore 
manuscripts have been reported.The total number of digitized manuscripts available across the country is 
over 8 lakh, out of which, more than 3.90 lakh manuscripts are available on Gyan Bharatam portal at 
present for public access in view mode. 

 
(b) & (c) Gyan Bharatam, is a Pan-India initiative covering cataloguing, conservation, digitization and 
publication of manuscripts identified across the country. For effective implementation, a framework of 
Cluster Centres and Independent Centres has been envisaged. These centres are provided financial 
assistance in form of grant-in-aid to undertake manuscript related activities as elaborated above. States / 
UTs have also been onboarded to act as the Nodal Coordinating Authority for the mission’s 
implementation and review within the State / UT concerned. Financial support to the States / UTs and 
their repositories is considered on case-to-case basisand in accordance with the applicableframework, 
operational requirements and availability of funds.  
(d) Under the Gyan Bharatam Mission, two centers located in Odisha namely SARASVATI, Bhadrak 
(Sanskrit Academy of Research for Advanced Society Through Vedic and Allied Tradition of India) and 
the Department of Sanskrit, Utkal University, Bhubaneswar have been onboarded. During the National 
Manuscript Survey, 78,056 manuscripts have been reported from Odisha. Further, 800 manuscripts have 
been conserved and 848 manuscripts digitized. Grant to the tune of Rs.28 Lakh has been released to 
SARASVATI, Bhadrak, Odisha in February, 2026 to carry out manuscript related activities. 
So far as Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu is concerned, out of the total 1,41,652 manuscripts reported in Tamil 
Nadu, 47,496 manuscripts have been reported from the Saraswathi Mahal Library, Thanjavur during the 
National Manuscript Survey.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 27TH JULY, 2026 
 
STATUS OF FUNCTIONAL EMPLOYMENT EXCHANGES AND MCCS 
 
1279.      SHRI APPALANAIDU KALISETTI: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the total number of Employment Exchanges/Model 
Career Centres (MCCs)  currently operational in the country, 
State/UT-wise; 
(b) the total number of job -seekers registered with Employment 
Exchanges/MCCs during each  of the last five years and current 
year, year and State/UT -wise, along with district -wise for Andhra 
Pradesh; 
(c) the details of the total sanctioned strength and actual number of 
personnel working in  Employment Exchanges/MCCs, indicating 
their designation/job in the country, State/UT and role-wise; 
(d) the total number of Government and Private vacancies notified 
through Employment  Exchanges/MCCs in the country during the 
said period, year, State/UT and sector-wise; 
(e) the details of the number of candidates placed in Government and 
Private sectors during  the last five years and current year in the 
country, sector, year and State/UT-wise; and 
(f) whether the Government has undertaken any review or impact 
assessment regarding  share of placements facilitated in Private 
sector through Employment Exchanges/MCCs and if so,  the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): Government is implementing National Employment Service 
through a network of Employment Exchanges. Employment is the joint 
concern of the Central and State Government. Centre formulates 
policies, standards and procedures for operating employment exchanges 
whereas administrative and financial control of Employment Exchanges 
lies with the respective State/UT Government. 
 

 
Ministry of Labour and Employment is running the National Career 
Service (NCS) Portal for transformation of the National Employment 
Service. The NCS Portal is a one -stop solution for providing career 
related services including jobs from private and government sectors, 
information on online & offline job fairs, job search & matching, career 
counselling, vocational guidance, information on skill development 
courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a digital platform 
[www.ncs.gov.in]. 
As on 15.07.2026, there are 1008 Employment Exchanges in the 
country. Further, under the NCS project, the Government has approved 
407 Model Career Centres (MCCs), which also includes 370 Employment 
Exchanges, that have been upgraded as MCCs. State/UT -wise details of 
the number of Employment Exchanges and Model Career Centres may be 
seen at https://dge.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/Directory_of_EEX.pdf and 
https://www.ncs.gov.in/User_Manuals/List_of_Model_Career_Centers.pdf 
respectively. 
The State/UT -wise, district -wise and year -wise details of 
jobseekers registered, and number of vacancies mobilized on NCS portal 
(including through Employment Exchange/ MCCs) across the country may 
be seen at https://www.ncs.gov.in/_layouts/15/ncsp/ViewStaticReport.aspx  
Further, notifying final hiring figures is not a mandatory 
requirement on NCS portal. However, the job hiring data is available only 
to the extent as voluntarily reported by the employers.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
ESIC FACILITIES IN PUNJAB 
 
†1280. SHRI SUKHJINDER SINGH RANDHAWA: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Government is aware that the beneficiaries of the 
Employees' State Insurance  Corporation (ESIC) are facing 
difficulties in availing timely and quality healthcare services in  
various States of the country, including Punjab; 
(b) if so, the details of the complaints received along with the action 
taken thereon in Punjab, district-wise; 
(c)whether it is a fact that the beneficiaries have to depend on private 
hospitals due to the  shortage of specialist doctors, paramedical 
staff, essential medicines, modern medical equipment  and 
diagnostic facilities in several ESIC hospitals and dispensaries in 
Punjab; and 
(d) if so, the details of the steps taken by the Government to address 
the said deficiencies, upgrade the ESIC hospitals and dispensaries, 
set up new hospitals/dispensaries and fill up the  vacant posts in 
Punjab? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): Grievances, representations and issues raised at various 
fora are addressed expeditiously by the Employees' State Insurance 
Corporation (ESIC) in coordination with the concerned hospitals and 
dispensaries. Further, ESIC regularly follows up with the concerned 
State Governments for early settlement of pending reimbursement 
claims relating to primary and secondary medical treatment availed 
by ESI beneficiaries under emergency circumstances from medical 
institutions outside the ESI hospital and dispensary network. 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  Medical care in Punjab is provided through 01 ESIC 
Medical College & Hospital at Ludhiana, 01 ESIC Hospital at 
Ramdarbar, Chandigarh, 06 ESI State Run Hospitals at Mohali, 
Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur, Amritsar, Mandi Gobind Garg, Phagwara, 69 
ESI State Run Dispensaries, 03 ESIC Dispensary cum Branch Offices 
at Rajpura, Barnala & Ferozepur. To strengthen healthcare services, 
ESIC has accorded in -principle approval for setting up three new 
hospitals in Punjab at Lalru, Rajpura and Malerkotla. Apart from this, 
ESIC has also empanelled network of 139 private tertiary care 
hospitals and 9 Government Medical Colleges/Hospitals. 
Beneficiaries are referred to empanelled hospitals on a cashless 
basis wherever required services are not available in ESI 
institutions. 
  Recruitment of doctors, teaching faculty, nursing officers 
and paramedical staff in ESIC is a continuous process. Recently, 
appointment letters have been issued to 388 Insurance Medical 
Officer (IMO) Grade -II, 234 Assistant Professors, 1,577 Nursing 
Officers and 472 Nursing Officers. Further recruitment against 1,827 
paramedical posts has also been completed.

Scheme), PM e -Vidya, and Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) during the last five

-wise total funds approved and the corresponding central share , since inception, are given at 

Annexure-V. Details of State/Union Territory -wise central funds released under the PM-USHA 
Scheme, during the last five years, are given at Annexure-VI. 
Funds are released to the States/UTs as per scheme guidelines and instru ctions issued by 
Ministry of Finance, Government of India from time to time. 
   
(c): Under Samagra Shiksha funds are released to the State Government in lump sum as per 
approved Annual Work Plan & Budget and subsequent distribution of funds to District level is done

Details of funds allocated and utilized in Karur, Dindigul, Pudukkottai, and Tiruchirappalli districts,

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO:- 1282 
ANSWERED ON-27/07/2026 
 
Deployment of School Teachers as BLOs 
 
1282.  Shri Sribharat Mathukumilli: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Government school teachers deployed as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) or 
for any other duties relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls during 
the last three years, State/UT-wise; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed the impact of such deployment on classroom 
teaching, student learning outcomes and teacher availability in Government schools, if so, the 
details and findings thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has received any representations or complaints from teachers, 
school managements, parents or State Governments regarding disruption of academic activities 
on account of such deployment, if so, the details thereof and the action taken thereon; and 
(d) the measures taken by the Government t o minimise diversion of teachers from teaching 
duties, including deployment of alternative personnel for electoral work and the timeline for 
implementation thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of 
schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments 
and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, deployment of teachers and assignment of 
duties to them, including for electoral purposes, fall within the administrative domain of the 
concerned States/UTs. The Department of School Education & Literacy does not maintain 
State/UT-wise information regarding deployment of Governm ent school teachers as Booth 
Level Officers (BLOs) or for duties relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral 
rolls. 
Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in its judgment dated 06.12.2007, while 
upholding the authority of the Electi on Commission of India to requisition teachers for 
election-related duties, observed that such deployment should be undertaken in a manner that 
does not adversely affect the functioning of schools and the right of children to education. The 
Hon'ble Court further observed that, as far as practicable, duties such as revision of electoral 
rolls should be assigned during holidays, non -teaching hours or non -working days so as to 
minimise disruption to teaching-learning activities. 
 

In pursuance of the above, the Ministry of Education issued guidelines dated 13.09.2010 to all 
States and Union Territories advising that duties relating to revision of electoral rolls should, 
as far as possible, be assigned to teachers during holidays, non-teaching hours or non-working 
days. The same is reiterated to all States/UTs from time to time. 
The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 also emphasises that teachers should be enabled 
to focus on their core academic responsibilities and should not be burdened with excessive non-
teaching work, so that they can devote adequate time to classroom instruction, lesson 
preparation, student assessment and continuous professional development. 
Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided 
to States/UTs for strengthening academic support institutions, including the State Councils of 
Educational Research and Training (SCERTs) and District Institutes of Education and Training 
(DIETs), and for providing continuous academic support through Block Resource Centres 
(BRCs) and Cluster Resource Centres (CRCs). The Scheme also supports technology-enabled 
governance and digital school management systems to improve administrative efficiency and 
reduce avoidable administrative burden on teachers. 
Further, through P roject Approval Board (PAB) meetings, review meetings and other 
communications, the Department of School Education & Literacy regularly advises States/UTs 
to ensure timely recruitment of teachers, rational deployment and optimum utilisation of human 
resources, and to leverage digital platforms for streamlining administrative processes, thereby 
enabling teachers to devote greater time to teaching-learning activities.

Central University Infrastructure 
 
1283 Shri Brijmohan Agrawal: 
 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of Central Universities currently operational in the country, State -
wise, along with the year of their establishment; 
(b) the total number of graduate courses being offered across these institutions; 
(c) the total number of students currentl y enrolled in these higher education 
institutions; 
(d) the details of new universities established in the country under the recent funding 
schemes; 
(e) the details of eco -friendly campus projects and green -energy hostel currently 
under development in Central Universities; and 
(f) the comprehensive future expansion plan for upgrading higher education 
infrastructure in Chhattisgarh? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) There are 57 Central Universities presently operational in the country, out of 
which 4 7 Central Universities , excluding Indira Gandhi National Open University 
(IGNOU), are under the administrative purview of the Ministry of Education. The 
State-wise details of Central Universities along with the yea r of their establishment 
are at Annexure. 
(b) to (c) All Central Universities are statutory autonomous organisations established 
under the respective Central Acts of Parliament and are governed by the provisions 
of their Acts, Statutes and Ordinances made thereunder. The Universities are 
competent to take administrative and academic decisions with the approval of their 
respective Statutory Bodies. 
 
 

Presently, except Sindhu Central University, all Central Universities under the 
administrative purview of the  Ministry of Education are offering undergraduate 
programmes. At present, a total of 3,09,542 students are enrolled in 47 Central 
Universities. 
(d) During the last five years, two Central Universities, namely Sammakka Sarakka 
Central Tribal University in t he State of Telangana and Sindhu Central University in 
the Union Territory of Ladakh, have been established. 
(e) to (f) Central Universities have undertaken various environment-friendly initiatives 
as part of sustainable campus development, including rooft op solar power 
generation, solar water-heating systems, rainwater harvesting, wastewater and solid 
waste management,  plantation and biodiversity conservation . Further, the Ministry 
has also provided financial assistance to the Central University of Odisha for creation 
of a green energy building to support the infrastructure developed under the project.  
Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya, Chhattisgarh, has identified requirements relating 
to strengthening of campus drainage infrastructure, academic and residentia l 
infrastructure, and hostel facilities.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1284 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
  
CRAFTSMEN TRAINING SCHEME 
  
1284. DR. K SUDHAKAR: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has noted Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) issues like 88 per 
cent seat underutilisation, limited access for out -of-school youth and gender disparity in 
enrolment; 
 
(b)  whether the Government has taken any steps to address inconsistent practical training 
quality, low post-training placements due to industry skill gaps and lack of career guidance, if so, 
the details thereof; 
 
(c)  whether the Government is planning to integrate remote learning, digital infrastructure and 
achieve 100 per cent capacity with inclusive measures, specially for women and remote areas; 
and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a to d):  The Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development 
and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), implements the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through a 
network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for skilling the youth. 
 
At present, training under CTS is imparted in 170 trades through 13,856 ITIs (Government – 3,328 
and Private – 10,528) across the country. 
 
The enrolment in ITIs has increased from 9.51 lakh in the academic session 2014 -15 to 14.70 
lakh in the academic session 2025-26. During the same period, seat utilization has improved from 
54% in the academic session 2014-15 to 64% in the academic session 2025-26. 
 
To ensure better utilization of training infrastructure and resources, DGT undertakes periodic 
rationalization of training units with no admissions. Accordingly, in January 2025, 21,069 units 
comprising 4.49 lakh seats in ITIs across the country, with no admissions during the academic 
sessions 2018 -19 to 2023 -24, were de -affiliated. Further, in May 2026, 4,292 units with an 
aggregate seating capacity of about 90,256 seats, wi th no admissions during the academic 
sessions 2022-23 to 2025-26, were also de-affiliated. 
 
The trade curriculum under CTS is updated periodically in consultation with industry, academia 
and State/UT Governments to incorporate emerging technologies, modern tools, equipment and 
machinery. The CTS curriculum also provides for On -the-Job Training (OJT), enabling trainees 
to gain practical exposure in industry settings and bridge the gap between classroom learning 
and workplace requirements. 

Further, DGT has developed the Bharat Skills portal, which provides digital learning resources, 
including e-books, videos, question banks and other e-learning content, to supplement classroom 
training and improve access to quality learning material for trainees and instructors under CTS. 
 
To promote greater participation of women in vocational training, 30% of the seats in Industrial 
Training Institutes (ITIs) are reserved for women. Further, the enrolment of women trainees under 
CTS has increased from 87,819 in the academic session 2014 -15 to 2,20,814 in the academic 
session 2025-26, reflecting the increasing participation of women in vocational training. 
 
Further, DGT undertakes various outreach and awareness initiatives to improve seat utilization 
under CTS and promote awareness among youth, parents and local communities about skilling 
opportunities and employment prospects under the ITI ecosystem.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1286 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
PENSION SCHEME FOR LANDLESS AGRICULTURAL LABOURERS 
 
†1286. SHRI VIJAY BAGHEL: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether any pension scheme is implemented for landless 
agriculture labourers by the Government; 
(b)if so, the details thereof; 
(c)the details of the total number of landless agriculture labourers in 
the State of Chhattisgarh at present; 
(d)whether there is any provision to provide minimum wages to 
agriculture labourers by the Government; 
(e)if so, the details thereof; and 
(f)if not, whether the Government proposes to implement the same? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): The Government runs Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan -
Dhan (PM -SYM), a pension scheme for providing social security to 
unorganised workers  including landless agriculture labourer. 
  The PM-SYM scheme was launched in February, 2019 in 
order to provide old age protection to the workers of the unorganised 
sector such as const ruction workers, home -based workers, street 
vendors, domestic workers and other similar categories. This is a 
voluntary and contributory pension scheme. Under the scheme, a 
monthly assured pension of Rs. 3000/ - is provided to unorganised 
workers after attaining the age of 60 years, and the spouse is eligible 
for 50% of the pension as family pension. Workers in the age group of 
18–40 years whose monthly income is Rs. 15,000/ - or less and who 
are not members of EPFO/ESIC/NPS (Government funded) and are not 
income tax payers are eligible to join the scheme. The monthly 
contribution by the beneficiary ranges from Rs. 55/ - to Rs. 200/ - 
depending upon the entry age of the beneficiary. Under the  scheme,  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
an equal matching contribution is paid by the Central Government. 
Enrolment in the scheme is done through the Common Service 
Centres (CSCs), which have a network of about 4 lakh centres across 
the country. Eligible unorganised workers can also self -enrol b y 
visiting the portal www.maandhan.in. 
   The number of Agricultural labourers registered on 
eShram portal (on a self -declared basis) in the state of Chhattisgarh 
is approximately 61 lakh as on 22.07.2026. 
 
  Under the provisions of the Code on Wages, 2019, both the 
Central Government and the State Governments are empowered to 
fix, review and revise minimum rates of wages for employees 
employed in scheduled employments under their respective 
jurisdictions. Ac cordingly, the appropriate Government fixes the 
minimum rates of wages for agricultural labourers falling within its 
jurisdiction.

Credit- Deposit Ratio of Banks in Uttar Pradesh 
 
† 1288. SHRI ARUN GOVIL: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the current credit -deposit ratio of banks in Uttar Pradesh along with the year -wise credit-
deposit ratio during the last ten years, year-wise; 
(b) the details of the action plan of the Government to improve the credit -deposit ratio in those 
districts of Uttar Pradesh where credit-deposit ratio is low along with the district-wise details 
thereof; 
(c) whether it is a fact that no bank in the cou ntry has established its Head Office in Uttar 
Pradesh, the largest State in the country whereas the Head Office of the bank plays a 
significant role in improving the Credit-Deposit Ratio; 
(d) if so, whether the Government has any plan to set up the Head Office  of any bank in Uttar 
Pradesh and if so, the details thereof; 
(e) the number of villages selected under the Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) in Meerut 
Lok Sabha Parliamentary Constituency that have bank branches; and 
(f) the plan of the Government to open bank branches in the above selected villages having no 
branches? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a): The current Credit - Deposit (CD) ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) in Uttar 
Pradesh stands at 52.01% as of 31.3.2026. F urther, the CD ratio of SCBs in Uttar Pradesh 
during the last ten years, year-wise is at Annexure-I.  
(b): The CD ratio of SCBs in Uttar Pradesh, district - wise as on 31.3.2026 is at Annexure -II.  
The State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC), Uttar Pradesh has informed that banks in Uttar 
Pradesh, undertake various initiatives from time to time, to improve credit deployment, 
especially in low CD ratio districts. These initiatives include, inter alia, targeted credit expansion, 
strengthening district- level monitoring, credit outreach and awareness, support to Self Help 
Groups (SHGs), Micro- Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and One District One Product 
(ODOP) Clusters, process improvements and digital enablement for loan processing and 
coordination with various member lending institutions. 

Further, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has advised the banks to ensure that wide disparity in the 
ratios between States/ Regions is avoided in order to minimise regional imbalance in credit 
deployment and banks may review t he performance of their branches in such areas and take 
necessary steps to augment the credit flow. The Lead Bank of the district may discuss the issue 
of low CD ratio in all its aspects with the banks and also in the District Consultative Committee 
(DCC) forum. Special Sub-Committees (SSCs) of the DCC should draw up Monitorable Action 
Plans to increase the CD ratio in the districts having CD ratio of less than 40% and to report the 
progress on the implementation of the plan to DCC on a quarterly basis and through them to 
the convenor of the State Level. 
(c) and (d):  The Head Office of Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is located in Varanasi, Uttar 
Pradesh, while the Head Offices of Uttar Pradesh Gramin Bank and the Uttar Pradesh State 
Co-operative Bank are located in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. The credit planning and monitoring 
activities in a State are carried out through RBI’s Lead Bank Scheme, irrespective of the location 
of the bank’s Head Office.  
(e) and (f): Ministry of Rural Development has informed that unde r the Sansad Adarsh Gram 
Yojana (SAGY), a total of 10 Gram Panchayats had been selected in Meerut District. Further, 
as per the Jan Dhan Darshak (JDD) app, as on 30.6.2026, all inhabited villages i.e. 98,047 in 
the State of Uttar Pradesh are covered by a b anking outlet (Bank Branch, Business 
Correspondent, or India Post Payments Bank Centre) within a 5km radius.

Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of construction of hostels in Navodaya  Vidyalayas started in the

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1291 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 27.07.2026 
 
NDC Targets 
 
1291.  SHRI MALAIYARASAN D: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the progress made by Government towards achieving Nationally Determined Contributions 
(NDCs) under the Paris Agreement, including the targets relating to reduction in emissions 
intensity of GDP, expansion of non-fossil fuel-based electricity capacity and creation of 
additional carbon sink through forests and tree cover; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the progress made by various 
sectors, including power, transport, industry, agriculture and waste management, towards 
achieving the NDC targets and, if so, the details thereof including Kallakurichi constituency of 
Tamil Nadu; 
(c) the details of the measures taken by the Government during the last three years to accelerate 
climate mitigation and adaptation, particularly in climate-vulnerable States and coastal regions; 
and 
(d) the details of the monitoring and reporting mechanism adopted by the Government to track 
progress towards the NDC targets and India's long-term goal of achieving net-zero emissions 
by 2070? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI V ARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (d)   India’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) comprises of three quantitative 
targets namely the reduction of overall emission intensity of our GDP, enhancing share of non-
fossil fuel-based energy resources in installed electric power capacity and creation of additional 
carbon sink.  
 
India has achieved a reduction of 37.38% in the emissions intensity of its GDP in 2022 from 
the 2005 level, against the NDC goal of reducing emissions intensity by 45% by 2030.  The 
share of cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel-based sources 
crossed 50% in June 2025, thereby achieving the NDC goal five years ahead the committed 
timeline. As of 30th June 2026, non-fossil fuel-based energy resources accounted for 54.18% 
of the country’s total installed electric power capacity.  India has created an additional carbon 
sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent during 2005 to 2022, against the NDC goal of 
creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5–3.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent by 2030 through 
additional forest and tree cover.  The NDC targets for the year 2035 have been enhanced, with 
quantitative targets to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 47% from the 2005 level, 
achieve 60% cumulative installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy 

 
 
resources, and create carbon sink of 3.5 to 4.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent through forest 
and tree 4cover as compared to the baseline year of 2005. The NDC also includes five 
qualitative targets aimed at promoting sustainable lifestyles, adoption of climate friendly and 
cleaner path and enhancing adaptation capacity, etc. aligned with the goal of Viksit Bharat 
@2047. 
 
Our goal is to achieve the NDC targets at the national level, in line with the provisions of the 
Paris Agreement which calls for nationally determined contributions and national level 
reporting from the signatory Parties. 
 
The Government of India stands committed to implement its climate commitments through a 
whole-of-government approach. The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) 
comprises of nine national missions in specific areas of agriculture, energy efficiency, green 
India, Himalayan eco-system, human health, solar energy, strategic knowledge on climate 
change, sustainable habitat, and water.  Six of its nine missions focus on adaptation for 
enhancing climate resilience of vulnerable communities. All these missions are 
institutionalized and implemented by their respective Nodal Ministries/Departments through 
various schemes and programs across many sectors.  
 
Several measures have been taken to accelerate climate mitigation and adaptation under these 
schemes and programs.  The focus is to promote renewable energy, electric mobility, 
sustainable transport and habitats; climate resilient agriculture; water conservation; enhance 
energy efficiency; forest and tree cover; restore ecosystems; reduce disaster risks, etc.   
 
Some of the flagship initiatives are National Green Hydrogen Mission; PM Surya Ghar: Muft 
Bijli Yojana; Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM); 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) for clean energy technologies, including high-efficiency 
solar PV modules and Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries; initiatives related to Carbon Capture, 
Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) and Nuclear Energy Mission; and launch of hydrogen powered 
train which is step forward towards future ready and low-carbon sustainable transport.   For 
coastal regions, measures include, inter-alia, conservation and restoration of mangroves and 
coastal ecosystems, implementation of the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) regulatory 
framework, strengthening of early warning systems and disaster preparedness, and promotion 
of nature-based and ecosystem-based approaches to enhance resilience against cyclones, 
coastal flooding, sea-level rise and coastal erosion. The Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline 
Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI) programme, along with other initiatives under the 
National Coastal Mission, contribute to the conservation and restoration of mangroves and 
strengthening the resilience of coastal ecosystems and communities.   Further, aligned with 
NAPCC, 34 States and Union Territories have prepared their respective State Action Plans on 
Climate Change (SAPCCs), which facilitate climate action based on State/UT-specific 
vulnerabilities, priorities and circumstances.  
 
The Government has institutional mechanisms to monitor progress towards India’s NDC 
targets and the long-term goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070. The Prime Minister’s 
Council on Climate Change (PMCCC), Executive Committee on Climate Change (ECCC) and 
Apex Committee for Implementation of the Paris Agreement (AIPA) oversee the 
implementation of domestic climate actions, with periodic inputs from concerned Ministries 
and Departments. In addition, implementation of climate commitments is undertaken in 
convergence with relevant Government schemes, programmes and sectoral policies, which 
have inbuilt monitoring and reporting mechanisms. India also tracks and reports progress, as 

 
 
per the Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) under the Article 13 of the Paris Agreement, 
through its Biennial Transparency Reports, and National Communications, supported by 
national monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) arrangements.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-1293 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
TRANSLATION OF ANCIENT BUDDHIST TEXTS  
 
1293. MS. MAHUA MOITRA:  
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that several university-commissioned and private websites 
in China and Europe are publicly hosting the English language translations of ancient and 
medieval Buddhist texts which were originally composed in Sanskrit;  
(b) if so, whether these translations have been done in collaboration with Sanskrit universities in 
India;  
(c) whether the Government is implementing any scheme for publishing translations of ancient 
and medieval Sanskrit texts into other Indian languages included in the Eighth Schedule of 
the Constitution; and  
(d) if so, the details of the institutions involved in the implementation of such a scheme along 
with the progress made till date? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Culture has not received any such reference and does not maintain a 
centralized database regarding such translation projects. Further, the Ministry does not host the 
English language translations of ancient and medieval Buddhist texts composed in Sanskrit.   
 
(c) & (d): The Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (CIHTS), Sarnath, established with the 
mandate of restoring ancient Indian knowledge preserved in Tibetan sources and translating 
Buddhist texts into Sanskrit, Hindi, English, Tibetan and other modern languages, has restored 
and critically edited over 77 Indo-Buddhist Sanskrit works. The Institute has published more than 
340 scholarly titles, including over 60 volumes of the Dhīḥ Journal.  
 
Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (NNM), Nalanda while primarily devoted to the study and 
promotion of Pali language and literature, has also contributed to the publication of English 
translations of important Buddhist philosophical works, including Pramāṇavārttika of 
Dharmakīrti. 
 
Functioning of Sanskrit Universities does not fall within the ambit of Ministry of Culture.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-1294 
ANSWERED ON –27/07/2026 
 
IRREGULARITIES IN UTILISATION OF SAMAGRA SHIKSHA FUNDS 
 
1294. Shri Hibi Eden: 
 
     Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has received any complaints or reports regarding 
misappropriation, diversion or irregular utilization of funds released under the Samagra Shiksha 
Abhiyan (SSA) if so, the details thereof along with  the measures proposed to be taken to 
strengthen accountability mechanism and prevent misappropriation of funds released under the 
said scheme and to ensure timely delivery of benefits to eligible students; 
 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any special audit of Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan 
(SSA) funds, particularly those meant for welfare measures such as school uniforms, textbooks 
and other entitlements for students, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Government is aware of the recent inciden t involving the alleged 
misappropriation of central funds at Elamakkara Government High School in Kerala, where 
funds allocated under the Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) to provide uniforms to 
underprivileged children were allegedly siphoned off using forged  signatures and if so, the 
details thereof along with the reasons therefor; 
 
(d) whether it is a fact that despite the central funds being deposited into the accounts of 
Elamakkara Government High School in Kerala, in August 2025, not a single rupee reached the 
eligible BPL students, thereby affecting more than 527 children; and 
 
(e) if so, the details and reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b):  Education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and majority of the schools 
are under the domain of respective State and UT Governments. The Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme of Samagra Shiksha is implemented in partnership with all the States and UTs. 
Financial assistance is provided to all States and UTs for various components for 
implementation of the interventions under Samagra Shiksha as per norms. Accordingly, the 
annual plans under Samagra Shiksha are prepared by the States and UTs based on their 
requirements and priority and this is reflected in their respective Annual Work Plan and Budget 
(AWP&B). These plans are then appraised and approved by Project Approval Board (PAB) in 
consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial  norms of the 

scheme. The funds are released based on the fulfilment of conditions prescribed by Ministry of 
Finance such as pace of expenditure, receipt of commensurate State share, audited accounts, 
statement cumulative State share, statement on outstand ing advances, up -to date expenditure 
statement, furnishing of information as prescribed.  
 
This Department uses a comprehensive online monitoring system called PRABANDH 
(Project Appraisal, Budgeting Achievements and Data Handling) to monitor the releases a nd 
expenditure, besides viewing approved outlays and other scheme related information. 
Morevoer, the Central Government, through various forums, including Project Approval Board 
meetings, review meetings, regularly reviews and assesses the implementation o f the scheme 
by the States and UTs and advises the States and UTs to implement various interventions under 
the scheme for providing holistic and qualitative education.   
 
There are robust monitoring systems which include, annual audit by an independent 
Chartered Accountant selected from the C&AG/State AG’s empanelled list , a regular CAG 
audit, and concurrent financial reviews and regular meetings between Audit and State officials. 
The Manual on Financial Management and Procurement also assists States in streamlining 
implementation and financial management. Thus reinforcing accountability, transparency, and 
fiduciary oversight.  
 
Further, the SNA platform was established to streamline f und management and 
strengthen financial discipline. To modernize and further strengthen the system, the 
Government of India launched the new SNA SPARSH platform. SNA SPARSH enables direct 
electronic transfer of funds to end users and supports digital submission and real-time tracking 
of bills, reducing intermediary delays and enhancing transparency. It also supports a Just in 
Time disbursement approach, ensuring funds reach end users precisely when required and 
minimizing idle balances. 
 
State of Kerala has  informed that no special audit has been conducted specifically for 
distribution of school uniforms and textbooks under Samagra Shiksha. 
 
(c) to (e): As per the information received from the State of Kerala, funds for free uniforms 
were released on 18.07.2025 from the State Office to the school via district authorities. During 
subsequent verification (utilisation certificate process), it was found that the allocated amount 
was not utilised for the intended purpose, and a misappropriation of funds had o ccurred. 
Consequently, uniform assistance could not be provided to the eligible students.   
 
The matter was reported to the District Project Coordinator, and subsequently to the 
State Office. An FIR was registered at Elamakkara Police Station, Ernakulam City vide FIR 
No. 0008/2026 dated 13.01.2026. The case has been registered under relevant provisions of the 
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, including Sections 306, 336(3), 340(2) and 316(2). 
Immediate administrative measures were also initiated by the State office upon becoming aware 
of the incident.

WORKING CONDITIONS OF GIG WORKERS 
 
1297. ADV PRIYA SAROJ: 
  SHRI PUSHPENDRA SAROJ: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Government has conducted any study on the average 
daily working hours and earnings of gig and platform workers and 
if so, the details thereof, State/UT -wise, particularly for  Uttar 
Pradesh; 
(b)the details of the number of complaints received regarding forced 
logouts, account suspensions, arbitrary penalties and reduction in 
incentive payments by platform companies  during the last three 
years and the current year, year -wise, State/UT-wise and district -
wise for Uttar Pradesh; 
(c)whether the Government has assessed that earnings of gig 
workers are sufficient to meet  the minimum wage notified by the 
respective State Governments and if so, the details thereof; 
(d)whether any action h as been taken by the Government against 
digital platforms for  violating labour laws or unfair employment 
practices and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)the steps taken by the Government to ensure transparency in 
payment algorithms and fair working conditions for gig workers? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): No State/UT-wise study report on average daily working 
hours and earnings of gig and platform workers is available. 
 
  The Code on Social Security, 2020 has come into force 
on 21.11.2025 with the objective to consolidate and simplify the 
existing social security laws into a single framework and to extend 
social security coverage to all workers, including organized, 
unorganized, gig, platform and self-employed workers. 
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
 
  For the first time, the definition of ‘gig workers’ and 
‘platform workers’ and provisions related to the same have been 
provided in the Code on Social Security, 2020. Gig workers and 
platform worker s are outside the traditional employer -employee 
relationship. 
 
  The Code provides for framing of suitable social security 
measures for gig workers and platform workers on matters relating 
to life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and 
maternity benefits, old age protection, etc. The Code provides for 
setting up of a Social Security Fund to finance these welfare 
schemes. The Code also has provisions to constitute a National 
Social Security Board for the purposes of the welfare of gig 
workers and platform workers. 
  The Code has provisions for setting up a toll-free centre, 
or helpline or facilitation centres for unorganized, gig, and platform 
workers by the appropriate Government. These facilities will 
disseminate information on available socia l security schemes, 
facilitate filing, processing and forwarding of application forms for 
registration, assist to obtain registration and facilitate the 
enrolment of the registered unorganized workers, gig workers and 
platform workers in the social security schemes.

(b)  Funds are allocated by this Ministry Scheme-wise, not State/UT-

The Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development (RGNIYD), 
an Institute of National Importance under the Ministry of Youth 
Affairs & Sports, Government of India, does not conduct State- 
specific or district-specific training programmes. The Institute 
conducts training, capacity-building, orientation, and leadership 
development programmes for youth and youth stakeholders across 
the country based on programme objectives and nominations 
received from the concerned Ministries/Departments, organisations, 
and other stakeholders. Accordingly, no training programme has 
been extended exclusively to Thanjavur district. However, eligible 
participants from Thanjavur district may participate in RGNIYD's 
training programmes through the proscribed nomination/selection 
process under the respective national or regional programmes.

MINISTRY OF TOURISM

ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
SPECIAL TOURIST POLICE AND HELPLINE MECHANISM AT 
TOURIST PLACES 
 
†1299. SHRI BALYA MAMA SURESH GOPINATH MHATRE: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the incidents of crime (such as theft, assault, sexual 
harassment) against foreign and domestic tourists have 
increased during the last two years;  
(b) if so, the details thereof, State/UT -wise particularly district -
wise for Maharashtra;  
(c) whether the Government has reviewed the operation of the 
special Tourist Police service or helpline mechanism at major 
tourist destinations in Maharashtra during the last two years; 
and  
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM   (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d): Safety and Security of tourists is essentially a  State 
subject. State/UT-wise & Crime Heads -wise Cases Registered under 
Crime against Tourist Foreigners during 2023 & 2024 received from 
National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) is placed at Annexure. 
 
It has been informed by National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) 
that data on Domestic Tourist and District -wise information is not 
maintained by NCRB. 
 
Ministry of Tourism has been continuously taking up the matter 
with all the State Governments and Union Territory (UT) 
Administrations for setting up of dedicated Tourism Police to 

strengthen on-ground safety mechanism for tourists. With the efforts 
of Ministry of Tourism, the State Governments /UT’s viz Telangana, 
Andhra Pradesh, Delhi, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, 
Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha,  
Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim and Uttar Pradesh have deployed tourist 
police. 
 
Ministry of Tourism through Indian Institute of Tourism & Travel 
Management (IITTM) got a study conducted naming “Functioning of 
Tourist Police in States/UTs & Documentation of Best Practices”, to 
understand the requirement of tourist police and sensitizin g the 
tourist police towards the needs of the tourists, which was sent to all 
the States/UTs. A training module, as given by IITTM for imparting 
training was also forwarded to Ministry of Home Affairs, which was 
further circulated to the Chief Secretaries of all State Governments 
and UT Administrations.  
 
To develop a comprehensive framework, Bureau of Police 
Research and Development (BPR&D) commissioned a study on 
Tourist Police Scheme and formulated a comprehensive report. With 
the objective of implementation of Uniform Tourist Police across all 
the States/UTs to create a safer ecosystem for the tourists, Ministry 
of Tourism, in collaboration with the Ministry of Home Affairs and 
BPR&D, organized a National Conference on Tourist Police Scheme 
of Director Generals (DGs)/ Inspector Generals (IGs) of Police 
Department of all the States and UTs in New Delhi.  
 
Further, the helpline services set up by State Governments/UT 
Administrations enables tourists to avail immediate assistance in 
distress situations. In Maharashtra, the helpline No. 112, operates 
24×7 and provides prompt emergency response services across the 
State. In addition, as a part of the Ministry’s continuous endeavors to 
make travel for tourists safe and secure, the Ministry of Tourism has 
also set up a Multilingual Tourist  Helpline for domestic and foreign 
tourists to provide support service in terms of information relating to 
travel in India and to offer appropriate guidance to tourists in 
distress, while travelling within India.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1300 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
 
CONSERVATION AND MODERNISATION OF THE MUSEUM AND ART GALLERY, 
CHANDIGARH 
 
1300. SHRI MANISH TEWARI:  
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of the deteriorating condition of the 
Government Museum and Art Gallery, located in Sector 10, Chandigarh, including 
concerns relating to roof leakages, inadequate climate control, poor maintenance and 
deterioration of display infrastructure; 
(b) whether the Government has received any proposal from the Chandigarh Administration 
for the renovation, redevelopment or conservation of the museum complex, and if so, the 
details thereof, along with the estimated cost, present status and timeline for 
implementation; 
(c) whether any financial assistance has been provided by the Government for the 
conservation, restoration and modernisation of the museum during the last five years, year-
wise; 
(d) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the preservation requirements 
of the museum's collections and the adequacy of existing infrastructure for their 
conservation; and 
(e) the details of the steps taken or proposed to upgrade the museum into a world-class cultural 
institution? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) Yes. The Government Museum and Art Gallery, Chandigarh, has taken cognizance of the 
deterioration in certain portions of the museum building, including roof leakages during the 
monsoon, aging climate control systems, deterioration of display Infrastructure, and the 
need for conservation of this Grade-1 Heritage building. Periodic repair and maintenance 
works are regularly undertaken. The Civil Wing of the Engineering Department has 
initiated waterproofing of the building, which is scheduled for completion soon. 
(b) Yes. The Chandigarh Administration has submitted a Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the 
comprehensive upgradation, conservation, and modernization of the Government Museum 

and Art Gallery under the Museum Grant Scheme of the Ministry of Culture. The DPR was 
submitted to the Ministry of Culture on 05.02.2026, with an estimated project cost of 30.33 
crore. 
(c) No. 
(d) Yes. The preservation requirements of the museum's collections and the adequacy of 
existing infrastructure for their conservation are assessed on a regular basis by the museum 
authorities. The need for modernizing the conservation laboratories, HVAC systems, 
reserve collection storage, and exhibition infrastructure has been Incorporated into the DPR 
submitted to the Ministry of Culture. 
(e) The following steps have been proposed in the DPR to upgrade the Museum into a world-
class cultural institution: 
1. Building Conservation 
2. Interior Upgradation and Exhibition Display 
3. Fire Safety and Risk Management 
4. Security & CCTV Surveillance Systems 
5. Display and General Lighting (Including rewiring) 
6. Installation of a 15-Passenger Elevator 
7. HVAC/Air Conditioning (with 24-hour power backup and generators) 
8. Collection Storage (including compactors, cataloguing, digitization via 
JATAN/TMS, and publication of catalogues) 
9. Conservation of Collections 
10. Digital and Multimedia Enhancements (Including AR/VR, holographic displays, and 
an audio app) 
11. Conservation Laboratory Equipment Upgradation

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1301 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 27TH JULY 2026 
SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
STATUTORY COMPLIANCE AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE 
 
QUESTION 
 
1301. SHRI Imran Masood: 
 
WILL THE MINISTER OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS BE PLEASED TO 
STATE: 
 
(a) whether the Government has conducted any sector -wise and                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
State-wise assessment of the cases of violation of the provisions 
related to financial statements, statutory compliance and corporate 
governance by various companies in the country during the period 
from April to June, 2026;  
 
(b) if so, whether any separate statement of inspection, investigation 
and penal actions taken against listed and unlisted companies has 
been included therein, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Government has identified those companies which 
have repeatedly failed in compliance and developed any special                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
monitoring mechanism against them, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(d) whether the consolidated data on these cases is being made 
available on a public dashboard or portal; and  
 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS; 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA) 
 
 
(a) & (b) No such specific assessment has been conducted. The 
Central Government orders inquiries, inspections, investigations as 
per the relevant provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 based on 
complaints, references and information regarding violations and 
other non-compliances. The penal actions pending and taken by field 
offices against listed and unlisted companies are reviewed regularly.  

(c) With regard to repeated non -compliance, there is no special 
monitoring mechanism in light of the existing provisions of Section 
451 and 454A of the Companies Act, 2013. Section 451 provides 
higher punishment for repeated offences and prescribes that i f a 
company or an officer of a company commits an offence punishable 
either with fine or with imprisonment and where the same offence is 
committed for the second or subsequent occasions within a period 
of three years, then, that company and every officer t hereof who is 
in default shall be punishable with twice the amount of fine for such 
offence in addition to any imprisonment provided for that offence. 
Similarly, Section 454A provides p enalty for repeated default  and 
prescribes that where a company or an officer of a company or any 
other person having already been subjected to penalty for default 
under any provisions of this Act, again commits such default within 
a period of three years from the date of order imposing such penalty 
passed by the adjudicating officer or the Regional Director, as the 
case may be, it or he shall be liable for the second or subsequent 
defaults for an amount equal to twice the amount of penalty provided 
for such default under the relevant provisions of this Act. 
(d) & (e) No. However, adjudication is undertaken through e -
adjudication module and a ll adjudication orders are available in 
public domain. Consolidated data (company-wise) regarding ongoing 
enforcement matters against companies is not published on the MCA 
portal as that would impede the inquiry/investigation process. The 
general compliance status of enforcement action is available in 
Annual Report on Working and Administration of Companies Act, 
2013 which is uploaded on MCA portal.

RAGGING COMPLAINTS IN HIGHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS 
 
1302 Ms Sayani Ghosh:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the number of complaints of ragging received from higher educational institutions during 
the last five years, year-wise and State-wise; 
(b) the number of institutions against which action has been taken along with the nature of 
disciplinary and legal action initiated in such cases; 
(c) whether the Government has reviewed the effectiveness of the existing anti-ragging 
mechanism of University Grants Commission (UGC) Regulations, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has issued any advisory to State Governments to strengthen 
awareness, reporting and grievance redressal mechanisms for the prevention of ragging in 
educational institutions, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to ensure strict compliance with UGC Anti-Ragging 
Regulations by all higher educational institutions? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) State-wise and year-wise details of ragging complaints received from Higher Educational 
Institutions (HEIs) during the last five are given at Annexure. 
 
(b)  The University Grants Commission (UGC) has issued Show Cause Notices to 107 HEIs 
including 18 Medical Colleges in 2025 for non-compliance with the mandatory provisions of 
the Anti-Ragging Regulations, 2009. These notices highlight lapses such as failure to secure 
anti-ragging undertakings from students and parents/guardians, and non-submission of 
institutional compliance reports despite repeated advisories and follow-ups. 
 

 
 
The regulatory approach has remained corrective and preventive, ensuring that institutions 
rectify lapses and adhere strictly to anti-ragging measures, thereby safeguarding student 
welfare and campus safety. 
 
(c) The UGC has introduced the third amendment in 2016 to the existing Regulations on the 
curbing menace of ragging in higher educational institutions. The definition of ragging has 
been broadened. Further, there is greater awareness among students, which itself reflects the 
effectiveness of the regulatory framework in encouraging reporting and redressal. 
 
(d) Advisories are issued by UGC to HEIs twice every year to strengthen awareness, 
reporting, and grievance redressal mechanisms for the prevention of ragging. 
 
(e) UGC has taken action as per the UGC Regulations on curbing the menace of ragging in 
higher educational institutions, 2009. Anti-ragging measures viz. establishment of 24x7 
National anti-ragging helpline, anti-ragging workshops and seminars, mandatory inclusion of 
severe consequences of ragging in prospectus of institutions, mandatory online undertaking 
by students and parents every academic year, display of anti-ragging posters at prominent 
places in the institutions etc. have been taken to ensure compliance of the regulations.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1303 
ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
Exorbitant Fee Hikes by Private Schools 
1303. Dr. Raj Kumar Chabbewal: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the increasing complaints regarding arbitrary  and 
exorbitant fee hikes and various forms of overcharging by private schools across the country; 
(b) if so, the details of the complaints recei ved by the Government during the last five years,  year-
wise and State/UT-wise along with the action taken thereon; 
(c) whether the Government has issued any advisory to the State Governments for  constituting 
independent Fee Regulatory Committees or strengthening existing mechanisms for  scrutiny and 
approval of fee hikes and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to take any measures to ensure affordability and  protection of 
the interests of students and parents while safeguar ding the quality of education  imparted by private 
schools; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 ANSWER  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (e): Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution. Schools, other than 
those established, owned or controlled by the Central Government, are under the jurisdiction of the 
respective State Governments/UT Administrations. Therefore, matters related to the management of 
schools that are not established, owned or controlled by the Central Government are regulated in 
accordance with the rules and instructions of the respective State Government/UT administrations. 
 However, every child aged six to  fourteen has the right to free and compulsory elementary 
education in a neighborhood school. Section 12(1) (c) of the RTE Act, 2009 mandates reservation 
in private unaided schools for children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups to 
the extent of at least 25% seats at the entry level and provision of free and compulsory elementary 
education to such children till its completion.  Also, Section 13 of the RTE Act, 2009 clearly 
prohibits the collection of any capitation fee.  
Also, t he Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has established bye -laws that 
regulate various aspects of school administration, including fee structures for private schools 
affiliated with the board. The Bye -Laws require express approval from the School Ma nagement 

Committee or adherence to the process prescribed by the Appropriate Government for any fee 
revision. Also, the  CBSE has taken steps to prevent schools from exploiting parents through 
mandatory purchases. CBSE guidelines prohibit schools from compe lling students to buy books, 
uniforms, or stationery from specific vendors. This aims to reduce the financial burden on parents 
and promote fair competition.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1304 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026/ Shravana 5, 1948 (Saka) 
INCREASING INFLATION IN THE COUNTRY 
†1304. Shri Sanjay Haribhau Jadhav: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a)  the reasons for the increasing inflation in the country; 
(b)  whether the Government acknowledges that the rising inflation has had an adverse impact  
on the poor and middle class, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  the details of th e fiscal measures taken by the Government to control inflation during the  
last three years; 
(d)  the details of the revenue collected by the Union Government through taxes levied on 
petroleum products, year-wise; 
(e)  the coordination mechanism established with th e Reserve Bank of India to keep the  
inflation rate under control; and 
(f) whether the Government is considering to reduce taxes on essential commodities and if so, 
the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) and (b): The average retail inflation measured by the Consumer Price Index declined from 
5.4 per cent in 2023-24 to 4.6 per cent in 2024-25 and further to 2.1 per cent in 2025-26. Owing 
to the commodity price shock and elevated global energy prices stemming from the West Asia 
Crisis, a seasonal pickup in vegetable prices, and the expected unfavourable El Niño 
conditions, retail inflation rose to 3.9 per cent in Q1 of 2026-27. However, it is still below the 
Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) inflation target of 4 per cent.  

(e): The Government and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) coordinate closely under the 
monetary policy framework specified under Chapter IIIF  of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 
1934, to maintain price stability, while keeping in mind the objective of growth . The 
Government, in consultation with the RBI, has issued a gazette notification on March 25, 2026, 
renewing the existing inflation target of 4 per cent with ±2 per cent tolerance band for five 
more years, extending the current inflation target (IT) mandate through March 2031. Adopting 
a cautious and data -dependent approach, the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee, at its June 
2026 meeting, maintained a neutral stance and kept policy rates unchanged to balance the twin 
objectives of supporting economic growth and keeping retail inflation within the 2 -6 per cent 
tolerance band. The RBI has also estimated inflation for 2026 -27 at 5.1 per cent, below the 
upper tolerance band of 6 per cent.  
(c) and (f): The Government has been actively undertaking a series of measures to control 
inflation and mitigate its impact on consumers, particularly the poor and middle class.  Over 
the recent years, these measures include, inter alia , the augmentation of buffer stoc ks for 
essential food items, strategic sales of procured grains in the open market, facilitation of 
imports and export curbs during periods of short supply, implementation of stock limits to push 
more supplies of select commodities into the market, retail sales of select food items under the 
Bharat brand at subsidised rates, and above all, distribution of food grains free of cost to around 
81 crore beneficiaries under the National Food Security Act and increasing the  disposable 
income of individuals by exem pting annual incomes up to ₹12 lakh (and ₹12.75  lakh for 
salaried individuals with standard deduction) from income tax. Further, the rationalisation of 
the Goods & Services Tax (GST) rates , especially on items consumed by the common man, 
such as food products, household articles, medicines, medical equipment, agricultural goods 
and specified automobiles etc., supports affordability for the households. Some of the recent  
measures taken by the Government to ease the inflationary pressures include reduction of Basic 
Customs Duty (BCD) on crude palm oil, crude soybean oil and crude sunflower oil from 20 
per cent to 10 per cent in June 2025; on critical petrochemical products to Nil from 2 April to 
15 July 2026 ; on whole Tur to Nil  with effect from 4 March 2 023; reduction of Agriculture 
Infrastructure and Development Cess (AIDC) on Masur to Nil  from 13 February 2022 to 7 
March 2025; imposition of Export Levies on exports of petrol, diesel and Aviation Turbine 
Fuel with effect from 27 March 2026; reduction of Central Excise duty on petrol and diesel by 
₹10 per litre  in March 2026 ; and exemption of imports of raw cotton from BCD and AIDC  
from 1 June to 31 October 2026.  

(d): The details of revenue through taxes levied on petroleum sector products to the Central 
Exchequer for the last five years are as follows:

STATUS OF EDUCATION IN PUNJAB SCHOOLS 
1305. Smt. Harsimrat Kaur Badal: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Central Government is aware that 3000 Government schools in Punjab were 
either damaged or flooded during the year 2025 floods and that several school buildings in 
Fazilka, Ferozepur, Amri tsar, Gurdaspur, and Sangrur remained structurally damaged or 
non-operational months after the floods receded, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the current teacher vacancy position in Government schools in Punjab including the 
number of sanctioned posts that are unfilled, district-wise; 
(c) whether the Punjab Government has been advised to expedite teacher recruitment as 
per the Right to Education Act norms and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether any Central audit of learning outcomes in Punjab Governme nt schools, 
comparing first year and second year in power to the pre ruling State Government period 
has been conducted, if so, the details revealed in the findings regarding the actual 
improvement or deterioration in reading and numeracy levels? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): Education is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and majority of the schools 
come under the purview of the respective State and UT Governments. Punjab experienced 
severe floods during August–September 2025.  As per the Post Disaster Needs Assessment 
(PDNA) conducted by the Ministry of Home Affairs, a  total of 505 primary schools and 271 
middle/secondary/higher secondary schools  were reported as completely damaged, 
while 1,932 primary schools,  1,109 middle/secondary/higher secondary schools  and 141 
Block Primary Education Offices (BPEOs) sustained severe damage in the State of Punjab. 
 
 As informed by the State  Government of Punjab, i mmediate safety measures and 
temporary arrangements were undertaken , wherever required , to ensure continuity of 
teaching-learning activities. Repair, restoration, and rehabilitation works of affected school 
infrastructure were initiated on priority. 
 
(b) & (c):  As informed by the State Government of Punjab, t he current district -wise 
position of teacher vacancies in Government schools in Punjab, including the number of 
sanctioned posts that remain unfilled, is at Annexure I. Further, as per the norms prescribed 

under the Right of Ch ildren to free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, the prescribed 
Pupil Teacher Ratio (PTR) is 30:1 at the primary level and 35:1 at the upper primary level. 
The State of Punjab currently has a PTR of 18:1 at the primary level and 16:1 at the upper 
primary level, which is well within the prescribed RTE norms. 
 
 This Department, during the review meetings and project approval board meetings, 
emphasizes/advises the State  to expedite the recruitment process to ensure adequate 
availability of teachers. However, education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and 
the recruitment/deployment and terms/service conditions of teachers comes under the 
purview of respective State Government and UT Administration. 
 
(d): National Achievement Survey (NAS) : NAS 2021  was conducted to assess the 
learning achievement of students of Classes 3, 5, 8 and 10 studying in State Govt. schools, 
Govt. Aided schools, Private Unaided and Central Govt. schools.  The performance of 
students in NAS 2021 in the State of Punjab is at Annexure II. The findings of NAS 2021 are 
available at https://ncert.nic.in/SRC_2021.php?ln=en. 
 
 Subsequently, PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 was conducted to understand 
the baseline performance in the development of competencies at the end of the 
Foundational, Preparatory, and Middle stages at the district level for Grades 3, 6, and 9 
respectively. The performance of students in P ARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 in the 
State of Punjab is at Annexure III. The findings of the PARAKH are available at 
https://parakh.ncert.gov.in/.

SKILL DEVELOPMENT IN WEST BENGAL 
 
1306. SHRI ADHIKARI DEEPAK DEV: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether the State Government of West Bengal has participated in the Central 
Government sponsored skill Development Programme during the last three years and the 
current year; and 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof ? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) & (b): Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re -skill and up -skill training through 
an extensive network of skill development centres under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan  (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs), to all sections of the society across the country including the state of West 
Bengal. The details of these schemes are as follows: 
  
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY):  The PMKVY Scheme is for imparting skill 
development training through Short -Term Training (STT) and up -skilling and re -skilling through 
Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) to youth across the country including the state of West 
Bengal. 
  
Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme : The scheme aims to impart vocational skills to the 
non-literates, neo-literates and the persons having a rudimentary level of education and school 
dropouts up to 12th standard in the age group of 15-45 years, with due age relaxation in case of 
“Divyangjan” and other deserving cases. Priority is given to Women, SC, ST, OBC and 
Minorities in the rural areas and urban low-income areas.  
  
National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS):  This Scheme is for promoting 
apprenticeship training and increasing the engagement of apprentices by providing financial 
support for payment of stipend to apprentices. Training consists of Basic Training and On -the- 
Job Training / Practical Training at the workplace in the industry.  
  
Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS):  This scheme is for providing long -term training through 
Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) across the country. The ITIs offer a range of vocational/skill 
training courses covering many economic sectors with the objective to provide a skilled 
workforce to the industry as well as self-employment of youth.

MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE

Violations of Environmental Clearance Conditions 
 
1307. SHRI PUSHPENDRA SAROJ: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) the number of projects granted Environmental Clearance (EC) during the last three years 
and the number of projects found violating EC conditions, State and district-wise, particularly 
for Uttar Pradesh; 
(b) the details of the inspections conducted to verify compliance with EC conditions, along 
with the number of violations detected and action taken, State and district-wise, particularly 
for Uttar Pradesh; 
(c) the details of the projects against which show-cause notices, closure directions, or 
environmental compensation have been imposed for violating EC conditions, State and district-
wise, particularly for Uttar Pradesh; 
(d) whether any projects were allowed to continue despite serious violations of EC conditions, 
if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to strengthen monitoring, ensure strict compliance with 
EC conditions, and fix accountability for repeated violations? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) During the Financial years 2023-24 to 2025-26 a total of 1898 projects were granted 
Environmental Clearances (ECs) by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change 
(MoEF&CC) / State Environment Impact Assessment Authority Level (SEIAA) for projects 
relating to the State of Uttar Pradesh. Details of the ECs district wise are placed at Annexure-
I. It is mandatory for the project management to submit half yearly compliance reports, in 
respect of the stipulated prior environmental clearance terms and conditions to the regulatory 
authority concerned. Moreover, the same has been made digital and all such compliance reports 
are to be submitted online by the Project Proponent on the PARIVESH portal. 
 
The MoEF&CC, through its Regional Offices, undertakes post-Environmental Clearance (EC) 
monitoring and compliance verification of projects granted Environmental Clearance. The 
environmental non-compliance are addressed as per provisions under Section 5, 15 and 19 of 
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and Rule 4 of Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986. The 
implementation of these provisions are guided by the Standard Operating Procedure (SoP) 
established vide Office Memorandum dated 25.11.2022 for post environmental clearance 
monitoring and compliance of projects, which prescribes the mechanism for taking action with 
respect to the observed non-compliance. As per the SoP, on receipt of the inspection report 
from the Regional Office (R.O.), an Action Taken Report (ATR) is sought on the non-

 
 
compliances, if any, reported in the inspection report. If satisfactory corrective measure are not 
taken by the Project Proponent, actions regarding issuance of show cause notice (SCN), 
personal hearing, re-verification and concluding action is taken by the competent authorities. 
During the reporting period, a total of 479 inspections of Category 'A' and ‘B’ 
projects/activities were carried out in the State of Uttar Pradesh by the Regional Office on the 
basis of which necessary action in cases of reported non-compliance is initiated. Further, in 14 
cases SCN have also been issued. The Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board also undertakes 
inspections and action to ensure compliance of EC / Consent to Operate conditions as per due 
procedure.
