GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1372 
ANSWERED ON - 27/07/2026 
 
Vocational Courses in Government Colleges in Muzaffarnagar 
 
† 1372.    Shri Harendra Singh Malik : 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government is considering to introduce vocational professional courses in 
Government colleges in Muzaffarnagar, keeping in view the district's major industries, 
namely sugar, steel and paper; 
(b) whether there is any proposal to link the proposed Centre of Invention, Innovation, 
Incubation and Training (CIIIT) at Muzaffarnagar with the Indian Institutes of Technology 
(IITs) for promoting high-end research, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any specific guidelines have been issued under the National Education Policy 
(NEP), 2020 to provide internships for meritorious students from rural areas of 
Muzaffarnagar in local steel plants and sugar mills, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government is considering any proposal for the establishment of a new Central 
University or a multidisciplinary research institution in Muzaffarnagar district and if so, the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): Government of India launched National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 with an aim 
to provide holistic development of students. NEP 2020 envisages integration of pra ctical 
exposure and skill courses with regular programs. NEP 2020 also emphasizes the importance 
of industry-academic connect to enhance employability of students/youth.  
 
To achieve the objectives of NEP 2020 and to create a robust ecosystem of industry exposure 
in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), University Grants Commission (UGC) has issued 
Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Programme (AEDP) Guidelines. Further, to ensure general 
exposure of industry to technical education students, AICTE has made inter nship mandatory 
component of model curriculum/programmes approved by AICTE.  
 
The UGC had approved 04 Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) in Muzaffarnagar District 
Uttar Pradesh to offer skill -based programmes under the National Skills Qualification 
Framework (NSQF) during the academic year 2020–21. Under the National Apprenticeship 
Training Scheme (NATS)  of Ministry of Education , 02 colleges in Muzaffarnagar district, 
namely Shri Ram College and Sanatan Dharam College, have started AEDP courses and have 
signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with the Board of Apprenticeship Training 

(BoAT) (Northern Region), Kanpur, for providing     training to students. Further, a total of 7 
establishments / industries of Muzaffarnagar are registered with the BoAT (Northern Region), 
Kanpur for providing apprenticeship training to graduates under NATS.  
 
Government of India has also  established several premier Centrally Funded Institutions in 
Uttar Pradesh to provide high quality and multidisciplinary education to students such as Indian 
Institute Technology (IIT) Kanpur, Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology (MNNIT) 
Allahabad, Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University  etc. Government of India 
also provides financial support to State Governments under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha 
Abhiyan (RUSA) / Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) for specific State 
Government universities and colleges  to improve quality by ensuring their conformity to 
prescribed norms and standards. Under PM -USHA, a total of 6 units under the Multi -
Disciplinary Education and Research Universities (MERU) component have been approved in 
the State of Uttar Pradesh.  
 
Government of India has approved 204 Units in the State of Uttar Pradesh under various phases 
of the PM -USHA scheme including Rs 5 crore for Vijay Singh Pathik Government 
Mahavidyalaya, Kairana, in Muzaffarnagar district  to strengthen colleges component of PM -
USHA.  
 
As per information provided by Government of Uttar Pradesh, “Maa Shakumbhari University, 
Saharanpur”, a State Public University, alongwith its affiliated colleges, provides internship 
opportunities to students. Further there is no proposal to link Centre of Invention, Innovation, 
Incubation and Training (CIIIT), Muzaffarnagar with IIT.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1374 
ANSWERED ON- 27/07/2026 
CLOSURE OF GOVERNMENT SCHOOLS 
1374. Shri Anand Bhadauria: 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether widespread closure and merger of thousands of primary and secondary 
Government schools in the country in recent years has adversely affected the 
implementation of RTE Act, 2009 which guarante es free and compulsory education for 
children aged 6-14 in neighbourhood schools; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the data on such closures and mergers of schools in the country during the last five years 
State/UT and year-wise including district wise for Uttar Pradesh; 
(d) the extent to which the increased distance to merged schools affect enrolment, retention 
and learning outcomes, especially for girls, SC/ST, and economically weaker children, 
State/UT-wise; and 
(e) the details of corrective measures initiated by the Government to ensure full compliance 
with RTE norms regarding pupil -teacher ratio, infrastructure and access to schools as per 
RTE Act, 2009? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to ( c): Education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and the opening, 
merger/closing of schools is within  the purview of respective State Government and UT 
Administration. The National Education Policy 2020 underscores that although consolidation 
of schools is an option that is often discussed, it must be carried out very judiciously, and 
only when it is ensured that there is no impact on access (Para 7.4). The aim of the school 
complex/cluster is to ensure greater resource efficiency and more effective f unctioning, 
coordination, leadership, governance, and management of schools in the cluster. 

 
  As per the information provided/uploaded by the States and UTs on the Unified 
District Information System for Education Plus  (UDISE+), the number of Government 
schools in the country, State/ UT-wise for the last five years is at Annexure I. The district -
wise number of Government schools in Uttar Pradesh for the last five years is at Annexure 
II.  
 
(d): The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of girls, SC students and ST students during the 
last 2 years is at Annexure III, Annexure IV and Annexure V, respectively. 
 
 The overall Retention Rate for girls during the last 2 years is at Annexure VI.  
 
The Ministry of Education undertakes large-scale assessments to measure learning 
outcomes in schools across the country from time to time. In this regard, the PARAKH 
Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 (formerly National Achievement Survey) was conducted by the 
National Assessment Centre -PARAKH, NCERT under the aegis of the Department of 
School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education to measure the baseline performance 
under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 in development of competencies among 
students at the end of the Foundational, Preparatory and Middle Stages (Grades 3, 6 and 9 
respectively) of schooling. Nationwide over 21.15 lakh students, including SC, ST and OBC 
students, and 2.70 lakh teachers from more than 74,000 schools across 781 districts from 
all States/UTs participated in the assessment. National, State and District  level reports for 
PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 providing insights on variation in learning outcomes 
across social groups for all subjects assessed are available at 
https://dashboard.parakh.ncert.gov.in/en, a dedicated dashboard designed to disseminate  
the findings of the assessment.  
  
(e): This Department is implementing an integrated centrally sponsored scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha since 2018-19.  The Samagra Shiksha scheme has been aligned with the 
aims and objective of the National Education Policy 2020 and the Right of Children to Free 
and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009. Substantial improvements have been made in 
access across levels of school education. 
 Under Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for 
undertaking various activities for Universalization of School Education including 
opening/strengthening of new schools upto senior secondary level, construction of school 
buildings &  additional classrooms, development/strengthening of school infrastructure in 

northern border areas under Vibrant Village Programme, setting up, up -gradation and 
running of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas, setting up of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose 
Avasiya Vidyalayas, construction of hostels for PVTGs under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi 
Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN), construction of hostels under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya 
Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA) for unsaturated ST population, free uniforms to eligible  
children and free text books at elementary level, transport allowance and undertaking 
enrolment & retention drives. Special training for age-appropriate admission of out of school 
children and residential as well as non -residential training for older chil dren, seasonal 
hostels / residential camps, special training centres at worksites, transport/ escort facility are 
also supported to bring out of school children to the formal schooling system including 
support to complete their education through NIOS/SIOS.  Under the student -oriented 
component for the children with special needs, financial assistance is provided for 
identification and assessment of children with special needs, aids and appliances, braille 
kits and books, appropriate teaching learning materia l and stipend to girl students with 
disability etc. 
  In order to maintain appropriate Pupil -Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various levels 
of schooling, the Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs as per 
norms of the scheme . However, education is in the concurrent list of the Constitution and 
the opening, merger/closing of schools is within the purview of respective State Government 
and UT Administration - which are the appropriate Government under the RTE Act. 
Accordingly, matters relating to recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers 
fall within the administrative domain of the concerned States/UTs.

ANWERED ON MONDAY, JULY 27, 2026/SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Waiver of Loans  
1375. DR. D RAVI KUMAR : 
Will the Minister of FINANCE  be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the demand from farmers for waiver of  
agricultural loans availed from nationalised banks, particularly in view of rising farm distress 
and indebtedness, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether it is a fact that while several State Governments, including Tamil Nadu, have  
announced waivers of cooperative crop loans, no similar relief has been extended for crop loans 
outstanding in public sector banks, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the total outstanding agricultural loans of farmers in nationalised/public sector banks as on 
31 March 2026, State-wise; and 
(d) whether the Government proposes to consider a one-time waiver or restructuring of such 
loans for small and marginal farmers and if so, the details thereof ? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) and (b) To provide relief to borrowers in distress, Reserve Bank of India has issued Master 
Direction on Resolution of Stressed Assets, 2025 dated 28 November 2025 (updated as on 01 
July 2026) which inter-alia provides lenders the discretion to undertake financial restructuring 
of borrowers under stress, based on their Board approved policies and regulatory guidelines.  
State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC), Tamil Nadu, has informed that no crop loan waivers 
have been extended for loans outstanding with Public Sector Banks in the State of Tamil Nadu 
during the last three financial years.  
(c) The State-wise details of outstanding Agricultural loans in Public Sector Banks, as reported 
by Banks on ENSURE portal of NABARD, are given in the Annexure. 
(d) No proposal for one-time waiver of loans of small and marginal farmers is currently under 
consideration with the Union Government.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ESI HOSPITAL AT TANDUR 
 
1376. SHRI KONDA VISHWESHWAR REDDY: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Government has received any proposal or 
representation from the State  Government of Telangana, public 
representatives, the Employees' State Insurance Corporation  
(ESIC), workers' organizations, industry associations or any other 
stakeholder for the  establishment of an Employees' State 
Insurance (ESI) Hospital at Tandur in Vikarabad district of  
Telangana; 
(b)if so, the details thereof and the action taken by the Government 
thereon; 
(c)whether the Government is aware that Tandur is a major cement 
manufacturing hub with several large cement industries, including 
Cement Corporation of India, employing a large number of workers 
covered under the ESI Scheme to facilitate insured worke rs and 
their families; and 
(d)whether the Government proposes to establish an ESI Hospital at 
Tandur and if so, the  details and timeline thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): A representation dated 03.10.2015 was received from the 
then Hon’ble Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Shri Konda 
Vishweshwar Reddy, regarding provision of ESI medical facilities for 
factory employees at Tandur, now in Vikarabad district, Telangana.  
  ESIC Headquarters accorded in-principle approval in 2018 
for establishment of a 2 -doctor ESI Dispensary at Tandur. However, 
as the Government of Telangana could not operationalise the 
dispensary, the in -principle approval has since been withdrawn on 
20.02.2026. The Insured Persons and their dep endants are presently 
availing primary medical care through ESIS Dispensary, Sadasivapeta 
and ESIC DCBO, Sadasivapeta. 
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
  The number of Insured Persons (IPs) in Vikarabad district 
is 757 as on 31.03.2025, which does not meet the prescrib ed ESIC 
norms for establishment of an ESI Hospital. Accordingly, there is no 
proposal at present to establish an ESI Hospital at Tandur.

MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1377 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
NEW-AGE SKILLS UNDER PMKVY 
  
†1377. SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL: 
            SHRI BHUMARE SANDIPANRAO ASARAM: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
  
(a)    the number of beneficiaries trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana  
(PMKVY) during the last five years across the country particularly in Madhya Pradesh and 
Maharashtra; 
 
(b)   the details of funds allocated and utilized for implementation of PMKVY in the said States 
during the last three years and the current year; 
 
(c)   whether the Government is planning to expand the scope of PMKVY to Cover new -age 
skills like digital literacy, artificial intelligence, robotics or green technologies there under; and 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof along with the steps being taken by the Government to promote 
the participation of women, Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and other marginalized 
communities in PMKVY, State-wise including the said State? 
  
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) Under PMKVY, a  total of 36,44,663 candidates have been trained across the country 
during the last five financial years and the current financial year, including 3,93,767 in Madhya 
Pradesh and 1,75,389 in Maharashtra as on 30th June 2026. 
  
(b)  PMKVY4.0 is a demand driven scheme and there is no provision of fund allocation in the 
scheme to the States/UT. The details of funds utilized for implementation of PMKVY in the States 
of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra during the last three years and the current year is given 
below:  
 
State 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 2026-27* 
Madhya Pradesh 43.17 205.84 26.98 3.67 
Maharashtra 32.09 44.44 6.05 1.01 
* Up to 30th June 2026. Amount in ₹ crore. 
  
(c)       Under PMKVY 4.0, training has been standardized through the National Skills 
Qualification Framework (NSQF), aligning courses with industry needs and national priorities. 
Under the Scheme, training have been aligned to the requirements of new -age and futuristic job 
roles such as AI, Robotics, Internet of Things (IoT ), Semiconductor, Drone technology, Solar, 3D 
Printing, etc. as per changing requirement and marked demand. To meet emerging technology 
demands, 600+ new -age and futuristic courses have been introduced.  As on 30 th June 

2026, around 5.44 lakh candidates have been trained in  new-age and futuristic job roles under 
PMKVY 4.0 across the country. 
  
(d)       PMKVY is a demand driven scheme accessible to every section of society including 
Women, Scheduled Castes (SCs)/ Scheduled Tribes (STs) and other marginalized communities. 
The Scheme does not envisage separate State -wise interventions, instead, it provides an 
inclusive framework applicable nationwide. To promote equitable access to skill development 
opportunities, the Scheme has a provision of Special Projects which are targeted towards 
ensuring coverage of under -represented social groups - SC/ ST/ Women/ PwDs and geographic 
areas such as Aspirational Districts, Tribal districts, etc. Special attention has been given to 
women, tribal communities, and other marginalized groups in rural areas to promote their 
participation in the skill development programs.  
  
In order to improve inclusivity by ensuring that SC, ST, women, and other marginalized 
communities can undertake skill training and eventually access gainful wage and self -
employment, boarding & lodging and transportation facilities are provided as per Common 
Norms. For non-residential training, conveyance/transportation costs are covered for women and 
PwDs. Additionally, ₹5,000 is provided for assistive devices, aids, and appliances for PwD  
candidates. All candidates are also covered under one -year accidental insurance for additional 
social protection.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1378 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27TH JULY, 2026 
 
EMPLOYMENT GENERATION AND LABOUR WELFARE 
 
1378.      DR. ALOK KUMAR SUMAN: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of employment generated under various Government 
initiatives during the last three years and the current year, year -
wise; 
(b) the measures taken by the Government to strengthen social 
security coverage for workers in the organised and unorganised 
sectors; 
(c) the details of the progress made by the Government in 
implementation of the e -Shram portal and other related welfare 
schemes in the country, State/UT-wise including Bihar; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to introduce additional 
employment-linked incentive measures in the country and if so, 
the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to improve job opportunities 
for youth across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (e): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India 
are derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by 
the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017 –18. 
The PLFS methodology was revamped with effect from January 2025. 
The PLFS Annual Report 2025 is the first report in the revised series to 
present labour market estimates, covering the period from January to 
December 2025. 
 
As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated Worker Population 
Ratio (WPR) indicating employment on usual status for persons of age  15 
years and above has increased from 54.1% in 2022 to 57.4% in 2025; the 
estimated Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) on usual status for 
persons of age 15 years and above has increased from 56.1% in 2022 to 
59.3% in 2025 and the estimated Unemployment Rate (UR) has 
decreased from 3.6% in 2022 to 3.1% in 2025 in the country. 
 

The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram portal 
(eshram.gov.in) which is a One -Stop-Solution for unorganized workers to 
have access to various social security schemes, Ministry of Labour and 
Employment launched the eShram – “One-Stop-Solution” on 21st October 
2024. eShram– “One-Stop-Solution” entails integration of different social  
security/ welfare schemes at single portal i.e., eShram. This enables 
unorganized workers registered on eShram to access social security 
schemes and see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram.So far, 
fifteen (15) schemes of different Central Ministries/ Departments have 
already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram to extend benefits and 
access to social security, health insurance and accidental claim to 
eShram cardholders. 
 
The Labour Codes were enacted to meet need for comprehensive 
labour reforms that formalize employment, simplify compliance through 
digital integration, strengthen social Security and ensure workplace 
safety and equality. The Codes will provide universal minimum wages 
and social security benefits for workers. 
 
The Labour Codes also have several enabling provisions which will 
promote formalisation and employment generation including social 
security and welfare of the workers. Such provisions include, 
formalization of employment through mandatory issue of appointment 
letter, universalisation of social security by extending coverage to 
organised, unorganised, gig and platform workers to strengthen their 
protection against employment -related vulnerabilities and enabling 
greater adaptability to new forms of work like gig & platform work and 
technology-driven employment models. 
 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability is a 
priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing 
various employment generation schemes/ programmes in the country. 
The details of various employment generation schemes/ programmes 
being implemented by the Government may be seen at   
https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes. 
 
The Rozgar Mela is a major initiative aimed at prioritising 
employment generation. Since its inception, more than 12.5 lakh 
recruitment letters have been issued through 19 Rozgar Melas organised 
across the country. 
 

Government is also implementing Skill India Mission (SIM) to deliver 
skill, re-skill and up -skill training through an extensive network of skill 
development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. under various 
schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan 
Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme 
(NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs) in the country. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India 
to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills. 
The Ministry of MSME launched Udyam Registration Portal on 
01.07.2020 for formalizing enterprises, expanding access to government 
support and strengthening the MSME ecosystem. A total of 8.9 crore 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) have been registered on 
Udyam Registration Portal, including Udyam Assist Platform (UAP), 
providing employment to over 39 crore people across the country. 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has 
initiated ‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of 
IT Manpower for Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies 
including Artificial Intelligence. 
Additionally, the Government is implementing Employment Linked 
Incentive (ELI) Scheme named as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat 
Rozgar Yojana to support employment generation, enhance employability 
and social security across all sectors, with special focus on the 
manufacturing sector. The scheme with an outlay of Rs 99,446 Crore 
aims to incentivize the creation of more than 3.5 Crore jobs in the 
country, over a period of 2 years. The PMVBRY is a demand -driven 
scheme. Under part A, incentive amount of Rs 744.7 crore has disbursed 
to 13.18 lakh first timer employees; and under Part B, incentive amount 
of Rs 2068.84 cr has been disbursed to 83,535 beneficiary 
establishments. 
Further, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, 
is running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop 
solution for providing career related services including jobs from private 
and government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job 
search & matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information 
on skill development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a 
digital platform [www.ncs.gov.in].

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1379 
ANSWERED ON – 27.07.2026 
 
Implementation of National Education Policy 2020 in Assam 
1379. Shri Parimal Suklabaidya:  
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the progress made in the implementation of the 
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 in Assam particularly with regard to foundational literacy 
and numeracy, multidisciplinar y education and the use of mother tongue/local languages in the 
foundational stage, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of schools selected under the PM SHRI Scheme and the number of Eklavya 
Model Residential Schools sanctioned and operational in Assam, district-wise along with the steps 
taken to strengthen infrastructure, teacher training and vocational education;  
(c) the present status of digital education initiatives, including DIKSHA, SWAYAM and other 
online learning platforms in Assam, indicat ing teacher enrolment, student participation, internet 
connectivity, and availability of digital devices in rural, tea garden, tribal and flood-affected areas; 
and  
(d) the details of Central funds allocated, released and utilized for NEP implementation in  
Assam during the last three years, along with the major achievements, challenges and the roadmap 
for ensuring equitable and quality education across the State? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): The Central Government continuously reviews the performance of the States. Accordingly, 
it may be informed that after the announcement of National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020), a 
number of transformative changes have taken place in school education for its  implementation. 
Several initiatives have been taken and the centrally sponsored schemes namely, Samagra Shiksha, 
PM Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI), Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) 

and Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society (ULLAS) have been aligned with the 
objectives and vision of NEP 2020. 
 NEP 2020 gives the highest priority to achieving universal Foundational Literacy and 
Numeracy (FLN) for all children by Grade 2  and accordingly, the Department launched National 
Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat Mission) 
under the aegis of the NEP and aligned with centrally sponsored scheme of Samagra Shiksha for 
early learning across States and Union Territories. 
  Implemented across the country, a range of interventions have been undertaken  under the 
Mission. These include nationwide implementation of Vidya Pravesh, a three -month school -
readiness module for all Grade 1 students; large -scale teacher and school head training through 
NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement) ; FLN 
focusing on activity-based and child-centric pedagogy; provision of play-based and digital learning 
resources such as DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) ; Jaadui Pitara - a 
collection of Learning Teaching Material (LTM)  & e-Jaadui Pitara for children in the 3–8 age 
group; Primers developed in 121 Local Languages for foundational literacy and numeracy in 
mother tongue and teaching learning material for students.  
 Further, guidelines on co-location of Anganwadi Centres with primary schools, released on 
3rd September 2025, ensure convergence between school education and Anganwadis, supporting 
smoother transition from pre-school to Grade 1. 
 NEP 2020 stresses up on providing multidisciplinary and a holistic education across the 
sciences, social sciences, arts, humanities, and sports for a multidisciplinary world in order to 
ensure the unity and integrity of all knowledge. 
 The State of Assam has informed that foll owing major initiatives have been under taken 
for active implementation of NEP: 
 Development of FLN focused textbooks and Workbooks/Activity books under NIPUN 
Axom. 
 Integration of NCF-FS framework 2022 and experiential & play based learning methods 
into pre-primary and primary grades. 
 Teacher Training on FLN pedagogy and assessment under NIPUN Bharat. 
 Contextualization and translation of TLMs(Teaching Learning Materials) from the list of 
JaduiPitaara into 12 regional languages for effective classroom transaction. 
 Provision and orientation of Bal Vatika Teachers on contents of the e-JaduiPitaara. 
 Notification of the age of admission as six years for class I. 
 Development of six months certification course on ECCE for the Anganwadi workers/pre-
primary teachers having educational qualifications of 10+2 and above. 
 Alignment of medium of instructions across all four stages of education as per NEP 2020. 
 Introduction of local languages such as Mising, Deori, Tiwa, etc. as medium of instruction 
in select schools from t he academic year 2025. A total of 38390 schools in Assam offer 
education in the mother tongue up to at least grade V . 
 Emphasis on formative assessment through the use of Holistic Progress Cards  (HPCs) at 
the foundational level. For this purpose, HPCs have been contextualized as per local needs, 
by the SCERT. 

(b): Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) schools are being set up as NEP 2020 
exemplar schools and are expected to become the template for other schools. As of now, a total of 
13,092 PM SHRI schools has been selected from 33 States/UTs, based on prescribed minimum 
benchmark through UDISE+ data. This includes 382 PM SHRI schools(associated with the State 
Government) selected in the State of Assam. The details of district-wise PM SHRI schools are at 
Annexure-I.  
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs  has informed that  17 Eklavya Model Residential schools  
have been sanctioned to be set up across various district s of Assam. The details of EMRSs 
sanctioned and operational in Assam are at Annexure-II.  
To improve infrastructure, PM SHRI schools across the country  including Assam are 
saturated with components s uch as Building as Learning Aid (BaLa) feature , Jaaduipitara, child 
friendly furniture, outdoor play materials , additional  class room etc. in primary and elementary 
schools and furniture, fully equipped integrated science lab/physics lab/chemistry lab/ biology lab, 
smart classrooms, computer lab/ ICT Lab, skill lab, playground with well - equipped sports 
facilities additional  class room etc. for secondary and senior secondary schools.  
 
 Under the PM SHRI Scheme, strengthening of teacher training is done through District 
Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs). There is financial provision of up to ₹3.00 lakh per 
DIET for capacity -building programmes of PM SHRI schools, along with assistance of up to 
₹2,500 per teacher for training of subject teachers, principals, special educators, ICT teachers, and 
master trainers. School principals are trained in leadership, management, and compete ncy- based 
pedagogical planning. Teachers are also trained on the Holistic Progress Card, school safety and 
security, mental health and well-being, first-level counselling, and integration of ICT in teaching-
learning practices, thereby enhancing overall teaching quality and school leadership in PM SHRI 
schools.  
 
 Further, PM SHRI scheme, aligned with NEP 2020, has a provision to integrate vocational 
education into the mainstream curriculum at the secondary and senior secondary levels, equipping 
students with essential skills for the future. There is a provision of setting up of vocational and 
skill labs by providing tools & equipment, raw materials, trainers, in -service and induction 
trainings for trainers, hands on training for students, linkages with sector skill councils etc. 
Students gain hands-on experience through internships with organisation/companies. 
 
(c): Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing  (DIKSHA) is the one nation, one digital 
education infrastructure. All states/UTs have been onboarded in DIKSHA. This digital 
infrastructure is artificial intelligence based and is highly scalable. This infrastructure is also being 
utilized for creating Energized T extbooks (ETBs) and presently 7 754 ETBs are published and a 
total of 3.67 lakh e-contents are available on DIKSHA. 
 Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds (SWAYAM ) hosts content 
curated by premier institutions and is available free of cost with the approach of “Anyone, 
Anywhere, Anytime” Learning. There have been more than 20,000 deliveries of courses on the 
platform, with cumulative enrolments exceeding 6 crores since its inception. During 2025, a total 
of 1,11,322 students from the State of Assam were enrolled on the SWAYAM Portal. 
 Under the PM eVIDYA initiative, the existing 12 DTH Channels of SWAYAM PRABHA 
for School Education have been expanded to 200 PM eVIDYA DTH TV channels to provide 

curriculum-based educational content, particularly for learners who do not have access to internet 
connectivity. A total of 1,12,822 video contents, equivalent to 32,763 hours of telecast  has been 
produced by States/UTs and Autonomous Bodies in 45 languages, thereby facilitating equitable 
and inclusive access to quality education. As informed by the State Government of Assam, under 
the PM eVIDYA initiative 5 DTH TV channels has been allotted catering to students of KaShreni 
to class-XII and Teacher Education. 
 ICT and Digital Initiatives component of Sama gra Shiksha covers Government Schools 
having classes VI to XII. Under this component financial assistance is provided for establishing 
ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms in schools. The non - recurring/ recurring grant under ‘ICT and 
Digital Initiatives’ is available to the States and UTs as per norms of the scheme. As informed by 
the State Government of Assam, ICT labs, Tele -education and Smart Classrooms have been 
established across 10033 Upper Primary, Secondary and Senior Secondary Schools, effectively 
covering rural, urban, tea -garden and flood -affected areas . A total of 21,04,755 students and 
1,11,946 teachers have been covered under this initiative. 
(d):  Under Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided to States and Union Territories, 
based on their Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B), for strengthening school education 
infrastructure and improving access, retention and quality. The States/UTs follo w different 
approaches specific to different regions or communities based on various factors responsible for 
dropouts. The need for schools and also the infrastructural facilities in schools, to ensure retention, 
are worked out every year by the respective State/Union Territory on incremental basis depending 
on their need and priority and reflected in their Annual Work plan & Budget (AWP&B).
